item.research_question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?
item.processing_route: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration
item.test_conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h
key_findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).
Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.
Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.
Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.
Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).
Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).
Processed samples formed predominantly protective Al₂O₃ and Cr₂O₃, while as-cast samples formed nonprotective spinels like Co(Cr,Fe)₂O₄.
Activation energy for oxidation was highest for the SFP_1800 sample, indicating superior oxidation resistance.
item.mechanism: The enhanced oxidation resistance is attributed to the ultrafine-grain microstructure and high grain boundary density, which facilitate rapid outward diffusion of Cr ions to form a dense, protective Cr₂O₃ layer, followed by the formation of Al-rich inner oxides via inward oxygen diffusion; the high surface free energy also suppresses the formation of nonprotective spinel oxides.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: The ultrafine-grain microstructure is obtained using stationary friction processing performed at two different rotational speeds, 400 and 1800 rpm, for 5 min duration.
Processed samples rich in grain boundaries (GBs) promote internal oxidation to form Al-rich inner oxides.

The enhanced oxidation resistance of the processed samples is attributed to the microstructural refinement and homogenization resulting in the formation of protective chromia followed by Al-rich inner oxides.
